'items on that they had gestured' is wrong — relative pronoun after preposition 'on' with a thing antecedent should be 'which', not 'that'. ①②④ correct.
'makes the information encoded in that speech memorably' — 'makes O C' requires adjective complement 'memorable', not adverb 'memorably'. ①②③ correct.
'Adults which were told' is wrong — relative pronoun for people should be 'who', not 'which'. ①③④ correct.
'we then ignored the adults' memories' contradicts the study's purpose — should be 'tested', since the whole point was testing/measuring memory. ①②④ fit context.
'recall that event worse than if you don't gesture' contradicts the passage's thesis that gesture helps memory — should be 'better'. ②③④ fit context.
Statement matches 'Adults who were told to gesture...remembered more than adults who were told not to gesture' — True.
Passage says memory was tested 'immediately after the descriptions AND three weeks later' — tested at both points, so statement (tested only immediately) is False.
Matches 'we gave the adults no instructions about gesture' in the second experiment — True.
'if people gestured ___' refers to gesturing without being told, matching later text 'if people gestured on their own' — on their own (스스로).
Original text explicitly states 'remembered more...particularly several weeks later', directly matching option 2.

Option 3 (second experiment researchers clearly instructed participants to gesture) contradicts 'we gave the adults no instructions about gesture' — this is the false statement. ①②④ all match the passage.

'Producing gesture along with speech makes the information encoded in that speech memorable' directly matches option 4. Others (①no lasting effect ②static photos ③opposite direction) all contradict the passage.
'a fence swung shut' breaks parallelism with the list 'a chicken sliding..., a jogger bending..., a fence ___ shut' — should be 'swinging' (present participle), not past tense 'swung'.
Passage lists three kinds of things in videos: 'toy objects, animals, and people' — the non-living, toy-made one is 'toy objects' (2 words).
Last sentence: 'Producing gesture along with speech makes the information...memorable' — the condition is gesture produced 'along with speech' (3 words).
Parallel structure with 'a jogger bending down' and 'a fence swinging shut' — 'a chicken sliding to a policeman' uses the -ing participle form.
The passage centers on a memory experiment showing gesturing while speaking improves recall of events — matches option 1.
The concluding idea 'gesturing along with speech makes information more memorable' matches option 3 directly.
